## TL;DR

RepoOS now tells a runner engineer what happened to its handoff. Every pass,
failure and deferral updates a small persisted status record and queues exactly
one outcome message through the existing queued-message delivery, so the
engineer's next turn opens with "handoff passed — task is now in review" or the
failing step and reason. A new non-blocking `repoos handoff-status <id>
[--json]` command (backed by `GET /api/tasks/:id/handoff-status`) reports
`not_requested`, `running`, `passed`, `failed` or `deferred` with the current
step and reason immediately, without starting or waiting for a handoff. The
engineer mission now explicitly says to request handoff and end the turn, and
not to call the blocking `repoos review <id>`. Tests cover the store,
deduplication, message wording, the API route, the CLI, the prompt text, and
the existing agent deferral path.

## Work and rationale

The core design decision was to keep the outcome path separate from the
blocking `repoos review` command. That command is useful for a human or an
external driver who wants the failure reason in the shell, but it is exactly
the wrong call for a runner engineer: the turn that requested handoff is being
torn down while the server-owned finalization runs, so a blocking wait either
races the server or burns a 25-minute turn. The new path is deliberately
asynchronous in both directions: request-then-end-turn stays the default, and
the result arrives as a queued message on the next turn.

I added `src/server/handoff-status.ts` as a small, dependency-light store. It
writes one JSON file per task under `<cacheDir>/handoff-status/`, which is
gitignored bookkeeping rather than task metadata, so a status write can never
dirty main, a task branch, or a commit. The record holds the state, current
step, truncated reason, origin, a monotonic attempt number, an attempt key and
an `outcomeQueued` flag. Every write is best-effort: a failed disk write logs
nothing and never fails a handoff. Reading is synchronous and cheap, which is
what makes `handoff-status` genuinely non-blocking.

Attempt identity is the key to the "exactly one message" requirement. For the
agent path the attempt key is the runner's `runId`, the same identity the
handoff capability is already bound to. A replayed callback after a server
restart, a recovery replay, or a duplicate invocation therefore sees the same
record and does not queue a second message. Explicit non-agent routes generate
a fresh UUID per request, because a new Review click or board drag really is a
new attempt and deserves its own outcome. `finishHandoffStatus` refuses to
overwrite a newer attempt with a late result from an older one.

Both `handoffTask` and `finalizeReviewHandoff` wrap their `onProgress` callback
so each step transition advances the stored step, then call
`finishHandoffStatus` after the deadline race settles. That placement matters:
finished duration timeouts are real outcomes too, and putting the recorder
outside `withHandoffDeadline` means a timed-out finalization is reported as
failed rather than left "running" forever.

Message delivery goes through the server's existing queued-message machinery.
I added `AgentRunner.queueTaskMessage`, which queues without starting a turn —
the distinction between `send` and queue-only matters, because the engineer
has just ended its turn and should not be immediately resumed just to read
"handoff passed". The three server call sites (agent handoff, unified
non-agent handoff, and the agent deferral path) format one message from the
record and call the same `deliverHandoffOutcome` helper. The helper checks the
record's `outcomeQueued` flag before queueing and sets it after a successful
queue, so retries and resumes cannot duplicate it. The messages state the next
action: nothing after a pass, and fix plus request handoff again after a
failure or deferral.

The deferral path is a little different because no finalization runs at all.
When a handoff is requested while the user's queued messages are unread,
`agents.ts` already clears the request and records `handoff_deferred`. I extend
that branch to persist a deferred status keyed by the turn's `runId` and queue
the outcome message. The next turn therefore sees both the user's original
message and RepoOS explaining why the handoff did not start.

For the public surface I followed the existing `landable` shape: a read-only
GET route in `routes/tasks.ts`, a `CONTROL_API_MATCHERS` entry in
`api-route-parity.ts`, a command in `control-api.ts`, a case in the CLI switch,
and a help entry. A missing task returns 404; a task that has never requested
handoff returns `not_requested` with a 200, because that is a valid state, not
an error. The CLI exits 0 for every state including failure, since the command
reports state rather than asserting success.

Finally, the mission text in `agents.ts` now tells engineers to request handoff
and end the turn, warns them off the blocking `repoos review`, and mentions the
queued outcome and `handoff-status`. I kept the existing "they are synonyms"
wording so the pre-existing `agent-drivers` assertion continues to protect both
handoff forms.

## Approaches tried

I first considered deriving status entirely from existing artifacts: the
Activity log, the in-flight marker and the last check failure fields. That
would avoid a new store, but it cannot distinguish "never requested" from
"requested and finished" when logs have rotated or a server restarted, and
parsing free-text Activity is brittle. A persisted record is simpler and gives
the CLI a stable JSON shape.

I also considered firing the outcome message through `runner.send`. That would
have delivered it immediately, but it also starts a new engineer turn, which
contradicts request-then-end-turn and would spend a turn just to announce a
pass. Adding a queue-only method was the smaller, clearer change.

For deduplication I considered storing a hash of the message text, but attempt
identity is more precise: a genuine retry after a fix should surface its own
result, while a replay of the same attempt should not. The attempt key plus the
`outcomeQueued` flag expresses exactly that.

## Challenges and blockers

The main sharp edge was the check gate's existing automatic retry. A failing
check already resumes the engineer with the check output, so the outcome
message must be queued before that retry fires and must not be re-queued when
the retry or a later watchdog resume happens. Ordering the delivery right after
the finalization result, and deduping on the attempt key, handles both. The
other edge was the deadline: recording inside the finalization body would miss
a timeout result, so the recorder wraps the deadline race instead.

No human-only verification was needed. The change is exercised with fake
runners, fake configs and temporary directories, plus the existing handoff,
message-queueing and API-parity suites.

## Key learnings

The existing queued-message system is the right transport for any agent-facing
notification that must not start a turn; `send` and queue-only are different
operations and the difference is easy to miss. Attempt identity, not message
text, is what makes "exactly once" reliable across retries and replays. And a
new control-plane read is cheap when it shares the `landable` shape — route,
parity entry, CLI command, help text — while a bespoke API path would have
failed the parity guard later.
